subject: Post-demo follow-up: deployment path & GPU sizing pulse
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Ashley Brant <ashley@opticsoft.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jul 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: deployment path & GPU sizing pulse

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier, Ashley — great conversation. Quick recap and items we need to qualify to recommend the right deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and a starter dedicated sizing: 

Summary from call:
- OpticSoft is evaluating inference for real-time document summarization + search reranking across internal knowledge bases and customer support flows.
- You indicated high throughput during peak business hours and sensitivity around latency for chat experiences.

Immediate asks to unblock our dedicated sizing recommendation (helpful if you can reply inline):
1) Deployment preference: are you currently leaning Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), or Private VPC/on-prem for compliance? If undecided, state top 2 constraints (cost / latency / data residency / SLAs).
2) Throughput targets: what are your expected TPS ranges? Please share avg TPS and 95th/peak TPS during busy windows.
3) Concurrency: estimate number of concurrent end-user sessions generating inference requests during peak.
4) Token profile: average tokens per request (input) and average tokens per response; any long-tail heavy prompts (>2k tokens)?
5) Latency SLO: target p95/p99 response times (ms).
6) Regional preference / data residency requirements (e.g., us-west, us-east, eu).
7) Compliance considerations: SOC2/PII, on-prem requirement, or KMS/HSM for keys?
8) Timeline & budget: target POC start date and any committed budget window.

Attached is a quick dedicated sizing template — fill the TPS/token numbers and return, and we’ll turn this into 2 concrete SKU options (cost + expected P95 latency + failover plan).

Proposed next step: 30m follow-up after we receive the template (we can prep two scenarios: cost-optimized + latency-optimized).

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx (Excel, 120KB)
From: Ashley Brant <ashley@opticsoft.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jul 2025 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: deployment path & GPU sizing pulse

Thanks, Stephanie — appreciated the clear list. Answering inline below and attaching a small traffic snapshot: opticsoft-traffic-snapshot.csv.

1) Deployment preference: leaning Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput and isolation. We may consider Private VPC later for compliance, but initial POC should be Dedicated.
2) Throughput targets: avg ~200 TPS, typical peak ~1,200 TPS (30–45 minute busy windows), daily troughs ~40 TPS.
3) Concurrency: estimate ~60 concurrent inference sessions during peak; many sessions multiplex requests (longer chat exchanges).
4) Token profile: avg input 350 tokens, avg output 450 tokens; ~5% of requests hit >1,500 tokens.
5) Latency SLO: p95 target <= 300ms, p99 target <= 750ms for the majority of user flows.
6) Region: primary us-west (we have an office + users there); EU data only for EU customers (not in scope for POC).
7) Compliance: SOC2 required; keys managed in our AWS KMS. No on-prem requirement for the POC.
8) Timeline & budget: hoping to kick off POC mid-September; budgeted for a three-month reserved commitment if results are good.

Let us know what you need from our side; Ben suggested he’d draft GPU family options.

Ashley Brant
Head of AI Products | OpticSoft
---
Attachment: opticsoft-traffic-snapshot.csv (CSV, 48KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo follow-up: deployment path & GPU sizing pulse

Looping in technical context based on Ashley's numbers — quick internal note before we propose SKUs.

Key observations from their answers:
- Peak 1,200 TPS with avg token budget ~800 tokens/req implies heavy GPU utilization per request.
- 5% >1,500 token requests will affect KV cache hit patterns and batch sizes.
- Concurrency ~60 sessions suggests we should assume ~120 model inference slots to allow for batching + headroom.

Two sensible dedicated pool options to present (high level):
A) Cost-optimized: A100-40GB instances, 8 GPUs in pool (multiplexing with aggressive batching).
   - Assumptions: effective batching keeps per-GPU throughput ~150–200 TPS for their token profile.
   - Expected p95 latency: 250–450ms depending on burst profile; lower cost but tighter for p99.

B) Latency-optimized: H100-80GB instances, 4 GPUs in pool (less batching, more parallelism).
   - Assumptions: lower per-request latency; better for tail heavy prompts and KV-cache-sensitive workloads.
   - Expected p95 latency: ~180–300ms, better p99. Higher monthly reserved cost.

Operational asks to finalize numbers:
- Can OpticSoft share a token-distribution histogram (counts by token bucket) if possible? That will let us model batching efficiency precisely.
- Any strict p99 SLA target (they gave p99 <= 750ms but confirm hard cutoff).
- Will they accept a canary with scaled-down pool (e.g., 50% of final GPUs) for initial validation?

I'll draft a short cost/comparison table once we have the token distribution. Recommend we propose both options in the POC doc and call out fallback routing to Hosted for overflow.

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Ashley Brant <ashley@opticsoft.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: deployment path & GPU sizing pulse

Thanks Ashley — helpful detail. Next steps and small asks so we can turn this into a formal POC proposal: 

1) Could you attach a token-distribution histogram or a small sample of request lengths (counts by token bucket) — that will materially change projected GPU counts. If easiest, the CSV you attached is good; ask your engineering team to add a tokens-per-request column.
2) Confirm p99 SLA threshold you must hit for GA (Ashley indicated 750ms — is that a hard requirement or target?).
3) Are there any requests that require private-cloud-only data access for the POC? (You mentioned EU-only later — clarify for scope).

Planned deliverables from Redwood once we have those items (target timeline: 3 business days after token data):
- Two SKU proposals (Cost-optimized on A100 vs Latency-optimized on H100) with per-month reserved cost, expected p95/p99 latencies, recommended autoscaling guardrails, and routing/fallback policy (Hosted overflow).
- A short runbook for the POC (onboarding checklist, monitoring dashboards we’ll provision, success criteria).
- Proposal for a 2-week canary (scaled pool) to validate latency and cost curves before committing to full reserved capacity.

Propose a 30-minute sync next Thursday or Friday to review the SKU options. Available windows: Thu 9–11am PT, Fri 12–3pm PT.

If you’re ready I’ll convert Ben’s notes into a tidy comparison and DocuSign packet for the POC statement of work (link below once ready).

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
